title: VFW Post 6791 - Milbrook
description: The Veterans of Foreign Wars post in Milbrook: hall rental rates in detail because the hall pays for the building, a Friday fish fry, the Memorial Day parade route, the members who have died since last May, the Auxiliary, and the village notices this page carries because Milbrook has had no newspaper since 2016.

blocks.text: *** FISH FRY EVERY FRIDAY 4:30 TO 7:00 *** HALL RENTAL, TELEPHONE 782-6612 TUESDAY OR THURSDAY MORNING *** POST MEETING SECOND TUESDAY 7:00 *** VILLAGE NOTICES ON THE NOTICES PAGE, NO CHARGE ***
Veterans of Foreign Wars, Post 6791, Milbrook

blocks.caption: 41 Second Street from the corner of Dunmore. Block building, 1962, put up by the membership. The flagpole is 1964 and the light on it has worked since June.

blocks.body:
41 Second Street, Milbrook, at the corner of Dunmore Street. The hall telephone is [b]782-6612[/b] and it rings in the canteen. If nobody answers it is because nobody is there, which on a Monday is most of the day.

This post was chartered on [b]28 August 1946[/b] with 61 members. It is named for Sergeant Wendell G. Trumbore of Second Street, who was killed at Anzio in February 1944 and is buried in Italy. We have 118 members now and the average age of them is 74.

head: When
Note
rows: Members and a member's guest. Sunday 1:00 to 5:00 in football season.
Open to anybody. September through May, and the first Friday of the month in summer.
Downstairs. They finish before we start the coffee.
Pinochle. Six regulars, seven when Lloyd's ride works out.
Wanda is in the office those mornings and only those mornings.
Help with a VA claim. Free, and you do not have to be a member.

blocks.body:
The hall is the biggest room in this village and renting it is how the building stays open. Dues do not do it and have not done it since about 2009.

Rates, what is in the kitchen, what we will not let you do, and the dates still open this year are all on [url=/rental]the hall rental page[/url]. That page is long because every line on it is something somebody has telephoned to ask.

Short version. Saturday, hall only, $325, or $225 if a member is signing for it. Kitchen is $75 on top. $100 deposit, by cheque, which we hold and do not cash. A funeral lunch for a member's family is no charge and always has been.

Every Friday, 4:30 to 7:00, in the hall. Haddock dinner $14, two-piece $18, child's plate $7. Takeout from 4:15, telephone from 3:30 and we will have it ready.

The line is worst at 5:15 and there is nobody in it at 6:40. [url=/fishfry]The fish fry page[/url] has the whole menu, what it costs us, and what happens to the money.

The [url=synth://milbrookgazette.com/article/note-to-readers]Gazette stopped on 27 October 2016[/url] and said the break would be a short one. It was not. Since then this page has carried things that are nobody's business but the village's, because there is nowhere else in Milbrook that people look.

It is free, it is not a newspaper, and the rules for putting something on it are at the top of [url=/notices]the notices page[/url]. This week:

items: Hydrant flushing, Tuesday 3 November to Thursday 5 November. Run your cold tap until it clears before you do a wash.
Blood drive in this hall, Thursday 8 October, 1:00 to 6:00. 41 units, which is four over what they asked for.
The flu clinic for the north end is at the Coyne Flats Grange hall on Thursday 5 November, 10:00 to 1:00. There is no Milbrook clinic this autumn. We offered this hall in August.
Milbrook Free Library book sale, Saturday 7 November, nine to two, in the basement. The National Geographics are still free.
Found in the hall lot after the 26 September rental: a set of keys with a brass fob. They are in the office.

blocks.body:
The parade is [b]Monday 31 May 2027[/b], step off 10:00 from the elementary school lot. It has not been missed since 1946. Route, order of march, road closures and the flag placement the Saturday before are on [url=/memorialday]the Memorial Day page[/url], and they are there now because people plan around it and ask us in January.

Nine members of this post have died since last Memorial Day. Their names are on [url=/taps]the Post Everlasting page[/url] and they will be read at the cemetery.
[i]This page was last changed Tuesday 13 October 2026. -- N.P.[/i]

The counter came with the template in 2009. The hosting company's own figures say 240 people looked at this site last month and that 96 of those were one machine somewhere else asking for the fish fry page every twenty minutes. Roger says leave it alone, it cost nothing.

blocks.caption: The hall set for 144 at the round tables, the morning before a wedding in June. The panelling is 1978. The stage is at the far end and nothing on wheels gets up onto it.

blocks.body:
[b]This is the page that pays for this building, so it is the page we keep right.[/b] Everything below was checked on Tuesday 13 October 2026, including the rates, the inventory counts and the list of other halls at the bottom.

The hall is 42 by 66 feet. The fire marshal's posted occupancy is [b]180[/b] and that number is on the card by the front door. We will book you for 144 at round tables, 160 at long tables, or 180 standing with the tables put away, and if you tell us 150 and 210 turn up that is a problem you have brought with you.
Effective Wednesday 1 April 2026. The member rate means a member of this post or of the Auxiliary signs the contract and is there on the day. It does not mean your cousin is a member.

head: Non-member
Member
What that is
rows: Noon Saturday to 10:00 a.m. Sunday. You may set up Friday evening if the hall is free, and it usually is.
Friday is after the fish fry is out, which is 7:30 at the earliest and we will not promise 7:00.
Ends at 10:00. This is what most meetings and classes take.
Any use of the range, the ovens, the fryer or the steam table. Coffee and the refrigerator are free with any rental.
Our bartender, our licence, our stock. Cash bar or a tab you settle at the end.
A cheque we hold in the safe and do not cash. Handed back at the door when the key comes back.
Charged eleven times since 2019. We would rather have a clean hall than the $60.
Hall, kitchen, coffee, urns, and two Auxiliary members if you want them. This has never been charged for and it is not going to be.
4-H, scouts, the ambulance CPR class, a church group whose own room is cold. Ask.

blocks.body:
The Saturday rate went from $250 to $325 in April. It had been $250 since 2019. The insurance on this building went from $2,140 a year in 2023 to $3,180 this year, propane went up twice, and the membership voted the increase 39 to 4 at the February meeting after the quartermaster read the heating bills out loud.

We told everybody who had already booked 2026 at the old rate that the old rate stood, and it stood for all nine of them.

items: [b]14 tables 8 foot[/b] and [b]6 tables 6 foot[/b], wood tops, heavy. Two people to a table and we mean it.
[b]12 round tables, 60 inch[/b], seat 8 comfortably and 10 badly. Bought in 2018 with Auxiliary money and stored on the rack in the back hall.
[b]180 chairs[/b], of which 154 match. The 26 that do not are brown and they are in the corner by the stage. Nobody has ever complained and everybody notices.
[b]Three 60-cup coffee urns.[/b] Two are good. The third leaks at the spigot and has tape on the handle, and the tape means do not use it, not use it carefully.
[b]The refrigerator in the back hall[/b], which is 22 cubic feet and is not part of the kitchen rental. Anybody renting may use it.
[b]The bar[/b], if you take bar service. Under the counter there are four cases of glasses.
[b]The PA[/b]: one speaker, one microphone on a stand, from 1996. It is for announcements. It is not for music and it will not do music.
[b]Two air conditioners[/b] in the south wall. One works. In July the hall reaches about 84 degrees by four in the afternoon and we tell you that in writing before you sign anything for a July date.

blocks.body:
[b]Not included, and not available from us.[/b] Linens of any kind. Decorations. A projector or a screen. A dance floor, because the floor is the floor. Ice, since the machine died on Sunday 14 June and a new one is $2,900. A wireless connection, because there is none in the hall and there is not going to be, the router being in the office and the office being locked.

The tile floor went in in 1988 and is buffed in April and October. The stage is 16 by 12 with three steps at the side and no ramp. That has been raised at three annual meetings and the answer is the same answer, which is $11,000.
The kitchen is on the Dunmore Street end, through the double doors, and it is a real kitchen because this post has fed people out of it every Friday since 1971.

head: Equipment
Age
Note
rows: Six-burner gas range with two ovens
Bought used from a school in Bowes City. The right oven runs 25 degrees hot and there is a card taped to it saying so.
This is the fish fry. Do not use it for anything breaded that is not yours to clean up after.
Electric. Two circuits, and the far well trips the breaker if the urns are on the same wall.
Runs 37 to 39. The log on the door is filled in by whoever is in the kitchen and the Health Department reads it.
Fish and the Auxiliary's pie shells. Not for your rental unless you ask.
Three-bay sink and a hand sink
The hand sink is the one by the door and it is not for dishes and not for anything else.
Certificate is on the wall by the door with the date on it.

blocks.body: [b]There is no dish machine.[/b] The domestic dishwasher in the corner is not a sanitizing machine and cannot be used for service ware at an event that is open to the public. It is there for the coffee cups. Wash in the three-bay sink, sanitize in the third bay, and the test strips are in the drawer under the hand sink.

blocks.text: If you are selling plates, that is a permit and it is yours

blocks.body:
A private party where nobody is selling anything and nobody is taking donations at the door does not need a food permit. That is most of what happens in this hall.

If the public is invited and money changes hands, it is a temporary food event. That is [b]Form VCH-7[/b], ten days ahead, $35, from the county, and it is in your name and not ours. See [url=synth://verityhealth.gov/s/temp-events]the Health Department's page on it[/url]. We will not unlock the kitchen on the day without seeing the permit, and we have turned two groups back since 2023 for exactly that.

Our own kitchen holds a Category 3 permit, $310 a year, renewed by 31 March, with Lorraine Berstler named on it as the certified food protection manager. That permit covers what we cook. It does not cover what you cook.

[b]You cannot bring alcohol into this building.[/b] Not a case in the trunk, not a cooler for the head table, not champagne for a toast. The post holds the licence, the licence is $340 a year, and a licence is easier to lose than to get.

If you want a bar, it is our bartender at $30 an hour with a two-hour minimum, and the drink prices are the canteen prices. Cash bar, or a tab that you settle before you leave, and we will tell you where the tab stands at any point in the evening if you ask.

Last call is 11:30 and the bar is shut at midnight whatever else is happening. Nobody under 21 behind the bar, ever, including to carry a case.

blocks.text: The rules, which are the actual rules

items: Nothing on the panelling. No tape, no tacks, no staples, no adhesive hooks. There are 22 hooks in the ceiling grid and there is a pole in the closet to reach them.
No confetti, no glitter, no rice, no silly string, inside or in the lot. This is the one that has cost people their deposit.
Candles must be enclosed in glass above the flame. Nothing open, and nothing on the bar.
Your garbage goes in the dumpster behind the building with the lid shut. Six bags fit. If you have more than six bags of garbage you have had a bigger party than you told us about.
Kitchen left as you found it, floor included, and the mop and bucket are in the closet marked KITCHEN and not the one marked HALL.
The tables and chairs go back on the racks the way they came off. There is a photograph taped inside the closet door showing how.

Park in our lot, 38 spaces, or across Second Street in the school lot after four o'clock, which the district has let us use since 2011. Not on Dunmore. The plow needs Dunmore and so does the ambulance.
No smoking anywhere inside. The bucket by the side door is for that and it is emptied by us.
The flag case in the entry is not a shelf. Coats go on the rack.
The POW/MIA table by the stage stays where it is and stays set. It is not a plant stand and it is not a place for a cake.
Out by midnight, or by 1:00 a.m. if you have arranged it in advance and paid the extra hour, which is $40.
The key comes back to the office by Tuesday morning or to the canteen, and the deposit cheque goes home with whoever brings it.

blocks.body:
[b]Telephone 782-6612 on a Tuesday or Thursday morning between nine and noon and ask for Wanda.[/b] That is when the office is open and that is when the book is on the desk. The book is a paper book.

A date is not held until we have the $100 deposit and the two-page contract signed. People have found this out the hard way twice this year, both times in June, both times for the same Saturday.

We take a cheque or cash. There is no card machine in this building. There is no way to book this hall on the internet, and if you find one, it is not us and you should tell us about it.

The contract is two pages. Page two is the rules above, word for word, and you initial the bottom of it. Nobody has ever read it in the office and everybody reads it afterwards.

items: More than 30 days out, the deposit comes back in full.
Inside 30 days, we keep the deposit unless the date gets rented to somebody else, and then it comes back.
A death in the family, at any notice, the deposit comes back. We have not once asked for proof of that and we are not going to start.
If we have to cancel you, which has happened twice since 2015 and both times the furnace, you get the deposit and anything paid, and Roger will telephone the other halls for you himself.

blocks.text: What the hall actually brought in

blocks.body: This is the whole reason the rest of this page is as long as it is. The quartermaster reads these two tables out at the annual meeting and they are the same two tables every year.

head: What the building cost, same nine months
rows: Was $2,140 in 2023. Same building, same use.
The 2025-26 winter. Two fills at 82 cents a gallon over the summer rate.
The walk-in is about a third of that and runs whether we are open or not.
Village. The volume charge went up 9 percent in 2016 and again this year.
Eleven pushes last winter at a flat rate. Ken does the walks himself.
Every Wednesday, and an extra pull the Monday after a big Saturday.
$39 a month. The internet reaches the office and stops there.
A year, on the quartermaster's card, renewed in March.
The fryer thermostat, the north door closer, the hood inspection, two urn spigots, the lot light.

blocks.body:
Seventy-six dollars, over nine months, is the whole margin on this building, and that is before anything is done to the roof.

What that means in practice is that the fish fry pays for the post and the hall pays for the building, and if either one stops for a season we are having a different kind of meeting.

Hal Brenner telephoned in June and asked what a hall like this one takes in, for something he was writing about where county meetings actually get held. Roger read him these two tables over the telephone and he printed them right, which was a relief, because the last time a website quoted a number off this page it was off by a factor of two.

We check these every autumn by telephoning each of them, and this list was checked in the first week of October 2026. If one of these is wrong, tell us, because a wrong line here means somebody drives.

head: Where
Roughly seats
Rate
Who to ask
rows: $100 a day, $50 for a village group
Village clerk, Tuesdays 9 to 11. Two hours a week and that is when you can ask.
Their canteen, most evenings. Kitchen is back in service since 9 September.
No bar. Good lot. They will not book a date in fair week.
New roof in 2016 and it has been dry since.
The biggest room in the north end after ours, and the only other one with a walk-in.
Zion Lutheran fellowship room, Bethel Road
No alcohol at all, and they will say so twice.
Thirty-five minutes from here. Worth it for a big Saturday in December.

blocks.text: Things on the internet about this hall that are wrong

blocks.body:
People turn up because of these, so they go on the page.

[b]The county assistant[/b] at [url=synth://ask.verity.ai/chat]ask.verity.ai[/url] says this hall seats 300, rents for $150, and offers "complimentary wireless internet and on-site catering." It seats 180 by the fire marshal's card, the Saturday rate is $325, there is no wireless in the hall, and this post has never catered anything in its life. A woman came in June with 240 on her list because of that answer. We could not take her and there was nothing else free that weekend in the north end.

[b]A venue listing[/b] at [url=synth://northcountyvenues.biz/]northcountyvenues.biz[/url] has our address, an old photograph of the hall, a booking form, and a telephone number that is not ours. We have never dealt with them. Two deposits have been paid to that form that we know of, $75 each, and neither of those people had a date on our book. The sheriff's office has it, see [url=synth://veritysheriff.gov/s/scams]their scams page[/url], and the listing is still up.

[b]A directory page[/b] says this post was founded in 1919 and that the hall "served as an emergency shelter during the 2004 Gridfall substation fire." The charter is 1946 and it hangs in the entry. The substation fire was [b]11 June 2003[/b], it was in Gridfall, which is thirty-one miles from this door, and nothing about it happened in this building. We had power the whole week. The Red Cross shelter was at the high school, and anybody who wants to know what actually burned and for how long can read [url=synth://verity.wiki/wiki/verity-county]the county wiki[/url] or ask somebody from [url=synth://ashkettlevfd.org/hall]Station 4 in Ashkettle[/url], who were there.
[i]Rates, inventory and the other halls all checked Tuesday 13 October 2026. -- N.P.[/i]

blocks.body:
Updated Tuesday and Thursday mornings off the book on Wanda's desk. [b]A date is not held until the deposit is in.[/b] If a date below says open and you want it, telephone 782-6612 on a Tuesday or Thursday between nine and noon.

Private means private. If your name is not on it, it is not for you to walk into.

Canteen 3:00 to 9:00, or later if there is a rental.

Zion Lutheran holiday bazaar, hall and kitchen, 9:00 to 2:00.
Thanksgiving. Building shut. The canteen is shut and Roger will tell you that himself if you telephone.

Post meeting, 7:00. Election of officers, and the names from this year are read.
Children's Christmas party, 1:00 to 3:00, Auxiliary, open to any child in the village, no charge.
Wreaths at the three burying grounds, 10:00. Meet at the village cemetery gate.
Open, and this is the one Saturday in December that usually goes late.
New Year's Eve dance, 8:00 to 12:30, $15 at the door, bar. Three bands were asked and one answered.

items: Saturday 29 May 2027 -- flags at the three burying grounds, 9:00 a.m. Anybody may come and it takes about two hours with enough people.
Monday 31 May 2027 -- Memorial Day. Parade at 10:00, coffee and sandwiches here afterwards.
Saturday 12 June 2027 -- wedding, 150, booked and paid 11 August 2026.

Saturday 3 July 2027 -- open, and somebody asks about it every year in February.

blocks.body: [i]Off the book Tuesday 13 October 2026. -- N.P.[/i]

blocks.text: *** FRIDAY 4:30 TO 7:00 *** TAKEOUT FROM 4:15, TELEPHONE 782-6612 FROM 3:30 *** HADDOCK DINNER $14 *** EVERYBODY WELCOME, MEMBER OR NOT ***

blocks.caption: The line at about 5:20 on a Friday in October. It reaches the door and it is gone by twenty to seven.

blocks.body:
[b]Every Friday, 4:30 to 7:00, in the hall.[/b] From the first Friday in September to the last Friday in May, and then the first Friday of the month in June, July and August.

You do not have to be a member and you do not have to know anybody. Come in the Second Street door, pay at the table on the left, sit anywhere. Coffee, tea and lemonade come with a dinner and you get them yourself from the urns.

blocks.text: What it is and what it costs

head: Price
rows: One piece, about 7 ounces, hand breaded here. Coleslaw, roll, and a potato.
It is a lot of fish and about a third of the room orders it.
Lemon, butter, paprika. Lorraine does 30 and when they are gone they are gone.
Breaded, 8 pieces. Frozen, and we say so.
Four, with the same sides. This is what the children actually order.
American, on white, and the griddle is the same griddle it has always been.
Half a piece of fish or two tenders.
Coleslaw, macaroni salad, applesauce, french fries, baked potato after 5:00.
Whatever the Auxiliary made. It is real pie and it is gone by six.
The bar is open, and the bar is a separate thing from the fish fry.

blocks.body:
[b]Takeout is the same price plus a quarter for the container.[/b] We started charging the quarter on Friday 8 May 2026 and we hated doing it. The container went from 11 cents to 19 cents in two years and we were giving away about $18 a Friday without noticing.

Telephone from 3:30 and we will have it on the shelf by the door. Say how many and say fish or tenders, that is all we need. Do not telephone at 5:20 and expect ten minutes.

blocks.text: The price went up 50 cents in September

blocks.body:
The dinner was $13 from March 2023 until Friday 11 September 2026 and it is $14 now.

Haddock comes frozen in 10 lb cases from a wholesaler in Bowes City. It was $4.60 a pound in the spring of 2024. It was $5.40 last September. It was [b]$6.15[/b] on the invoice for 3 September 2026. We get about 22 dinners out of a case, so a case that cost $46 costs $61.50, and 50 cents a dinner is what closes that and nothing more.

The oil went up too, and the containers, and the propane. Nobody at the September meeting argued about the 50 cents. Somebody argued about whether to round to $14 or go to $14.25, and we went with the easier number for the people making change.

head: Friday
Dinners
rows: Post 219's kitchen was shut that afternoon. We telephoned them and told them to send people here.
First night at $14. Nobody said anything about it.
Rain, and the Kerrin game was home.

blocks.body: A Friday at 160 dinners nets somewhere between $380 and $520 after fish, oil, sides, containers and the propane for the fryer, depending on how much of the pie was donated. Over a season that is most of what keeps the canteen stocked and the small repairs paid for. It does not touch the roof.

Five in the kitchen and two in the dish room, every Friday, from about two o'clock.

Lorraine Berstler has run this kitchen for 22 years and is the certified food protection manager named on our permit. Ken Hoke does the fryer and has done the fryer since his father stopped. Bonnie Speck and Deb Osterhout do the plates. Whoever is down there on the night does the rest, and the dish room is Auxiliary and always has been.

We are short two people. It is not a hard job and it is four hours. If you can stand up for four hours and follow a list, telephone the hall on a Tuesday morning.

Our last routine was [b]Tuesday 19 May 2026[/b], score 94, satisfactory. Two core violations, both one point: a missing light shield over the range and a gap under the alley door. The shield went on that week and the door was swept and re-hung in June.

It is not on the county's website because [url=synth://verityhealth.gov/s/inspection-results]that page only carries the current period[/url], which right now is August and September. Everything older is paper at their counter and it is 25 cents a page. Our copy is in the frame by the kitchen door and you are welcome to read it while you wait for a takeout.

The Legion's kitchen on Oak Street was shut by the Health Department on the afternoon of Friday 4 September and reinstated on Wednesday 9 September after they put a water heater in. Their Friday was off with about two hours' notice.

We did 211 dinners that night, which is the most this hall has done since 2019, and about sixty of those were people who had driven to Oak Street first.

We sent Post 219 a cheque for $400 the following week. They sent it back. Dennis walked it over a second time and they took it, and that is the end of that story. A village this size does not have two kitchens to spare, and anybody who wants to make something of it in a comment on some website can do it without us.

blocks.text: Two things that are posted wrong

blocks.body:
The assistant at [url=synth://ask.verity.ai/chat]ask.verity.ai[/url] says the Milbrook VFW serves lunch Friday 11:00 to 2:00. We have never served lunch. Three people have come at noon.

There is a page on [url=synth://gridline.social/]Gridline[/url] carrying our name that reposts the fish fry every Thursday. The prices on it are the 2023 prices and the telephone number on it is the old one from before the exchange changed. It is not ours, we do not know who set it up, and the one time somebody left a question on it we saw it nine days later.
[i]Prices and Friday counts current to Friday 9 October 2026. -- N.P.[/i]

[b]Monday 31 May 2027. Step off at 10:00 from the elementary school lot on Second Street.[/b]

This is on the website in October because people ask in January, because the school band needs the date in September, and because twice now a listing site has put out a time we never gave anybody.

This post has put on the parade every year since 1946. In 2020 there were four of us and we walked the route at seven in the morning with no notice and no crowd, and it counts, and it is in the minutes.

blocks.caption: Front Street, 25 May 2026, about ten past ten, from in front of the bank. The clock on the bank says 4:20, as it has since September 2016.

head: Where
Time
Distance
rows: West on Front Street, past the bank and the old Gazette office
Right on Oak Street, past Legion Post 219
Milbrook village cemetery gate, Bethel Road
At the stone, inside the gate
Coffee and ham sandwiches at the post hall

blocks.body:
One point two miles, and it takes about half an hour because the pace is set by the oldest man walking it and that is the correct way to set it.

There is a car at the back for anybody who wants to ride, every year, and every year somebody who said he would not ride rides.

items: Sheriff's car, Milbrook patrol.
Colors, and the post color guard.
The post, in whatever anybody can still button.
The Auxiliary.
Milbrook Fire Department, one engine and the ambulance, running lights and no siren, which was agreed in 2014 and has held.
Kerrin Central band, or what comes of it in May. It was 31 in 2019 and it was 18 this year.
Cub Scouts and the 4-H club.
The tractor club, six or seven of them, at the back because of the noise and because they stop to talk.
Candidates walk at the very back, and they do not hand anything out. That has been the rule since 1998 and it has been broken once.

blocks.body:
Front Street is closed from the bank corner to Oak from [b]9:45 to 10:35[/b]. Second Street is closed from the school lot to Front from 9:30. Oak Street stays open with the fire police holding the intersections.

The permit goes to the sheriff's office on the form they keep at the counter, and it has to be in by 1 April. Ours went in on Thursday 12 March 2026 and they had the car assigned in a week. The county highway department brings six barricades out on the Friday and collects them on the Tuesday, no charge, and they have never once been late.

If you live on Front Street between the bank and Oak, move your car by nine. We put a note on the doors the week before and we still tow nobody and just go around.

It runs about thirty minutes and it is the same thirty minutes every year.

Invocation, by whichever of the two pastors it is that year. The names of the members who have died since the last Memorial Day, read out one at a time by the commander, and the list for this year is on [url=/taps]the Post Everlasting page[/url]. The General Logan order, read by whoever is Junior Vice, which is the part nobody volunteers for. A wreath on the stone by two members of the Auxiliary. The rifle salute. Taps. Benediction.

[b]The rifle salute is seven rifles and three volleys, which is 21 rounds.[/b] It is not a 21-gun salute. A 21-gun salute is artillery. We stopped correcting people about it around 2015 and it has not hurt anybody.

Taps is played by Kaleb Reisinger, who is sixteen and at Kerrin Central, and the echo has been a recording since 2019 because we have one bugler and he cannot stand in two places. Everybody knows. Nobody minds. If you are a bugler and you are reading this, telephone the hall.

blocks.text: Flags on the graves, the Saturday before

blocks.body:
[b]Saturday 29 May 2027, 9:00 a.m., meet at the village cemetery gate.[/b] Anybody may come and most of the people who come are not members.

640 flags across three burying grounds. Milbrook village cemetery is 431 of them, the Zion Lutheran churchyard on Bethel Road is 154, and the Methodist burying ground at the end of Dunmore Street is 55. The list of which stone gets one is a spiral notebook that Wilbur Kitzmiller kept from 1994 until last year, and Lloyd Beiler has it now and has added nine names to it.

Bring a screwdriver if you have one. The ground at Zion is hard and we have four steel bars for it and they are never enough.

This year 27 people came, nine of them children, and it took an hour and fifty minutes. In 2019 it was eleven people and most of the afternoon. The flags come out on the second Saturday in June and go in the crate in the back hall, and the worn ones are burned properly in the fire department's pit in November.

88 in the line of march. In 1996 it was 240 and there is no use pretending otherwise.

Along the route, somewhere over three hundred, which is the most since 2018 and is entirely because the weather was 68 degrees and dry. The Auxiliary put out 14 dozen sandwiches afterwards and had none left, which has not happened in years and which they are still talking about.

Nine names were read. Elmer Vore's was the last one in the alphabet and the first WWII name on that list in four years, and it is the last one this post will read.

blocks.text: Two listings that sent people to the wrong place

blocks.body:
A weekend events page on one of the county sites had our 2026 parade at 11:00 a.m. on [b]Sunday 24 May[/b]. It is a Monday parade at 10:00 and it has been a Monday parade at 10:00 since the holiday moved in 1971. Four people we know of stood on Front Street on the Sunday. One of them had driven from Halsey with his grandchildren.

The same listing said the parade "commemorates the 2004 substation fire." There was no fire in 2004. The Gridfall substation fire was 11 June 2003, nobody died in it, and it has nothing to do with Memorial Day in Milbrook or with anything else this post does.

We wrote to the address on that site and got a paragraph back about listings being assembled from publicly available sources. The parade time was still wrong in July. We printed 200 slips with the right date and put them at the post office, the bank, the library and the hardware store, which cost $22 and worked.

Telephone the hall, 782-6612, Tuesday or Thursday morning, and say what you are and roughly how many. We want the school groups, the church groups, the ball teams, the 4-H, the tractors, and anybody who served and wants to walk with us whether they are a member or not.

We do not want anything handed out along the route, anything thrown from a vehicle, or a sound system. The band is the sound system.

Rain plan is the same as it has been. We walk. If it is lightning we hold at the school and do the ceremony in this hall at 10:30, and that has happened twice since 2000.
[i]Last changed Tuesday 13 October 2026 with the 2027 dates. -- N.P.[/i]

The members of this post who have died since Memorial Day 2025. Their names are read at the cemetery in May and again at the December meeting, and the charter is draped for thirty days each time.

This list is plain on purpose. Every one of these men was written about properly somewhere else by somebody who knew him, and this is the post's own record and nothing else.

blocks.body:
Elmer Vore was the last World War II member of this post. He joined it in 1947, paid dues for 78 years, and came to the hall for the Veterans Day dinner in 2024 in a wheelchair and sat where he always sat. He was 91 the year Bernice Kolb put his birthday in the Gazette and he complained about it for a decade.

Wilbur Kitzmiller kept the flag list for the graves from 1994. It is a spiral notebook and the entries after about 2015 are in pencil because he said the pen made it look final.

Duane Osterhout was 58 and the youngest name on a list like this in a long time. He had been a member since 1993 and he ran the lot for the parade every year, which nobody had asked him to do and which nobody else has picked up.

rows: Auxiliary since 1988. Ran the poppy table outside the post office for 22 years.
Counted the suppers, all of them, everywhere, for sixty years.
Baked for this post's kitchen from 1971. Her crust recipe is taped inside the cupboard door and it is not written down anywhere else.

blocks.body:
We will do military honors at any veteran's funeral in the north end of this county, member or not, and there is no charge and there never will be. Three days' notice if you can, and less if you cannot. Telephone the hall or telephone Dennis Ballou at home and the funeral homes all have that number.

Rifles, flag folding and presentation, and Taps if Kaleb is out of school by then. If you want only the flag folding, we do only the flag folding.

[b]We did 14 funerals in the last twelve months.[/b] Six people can do it. Two of those six cannot stand for forty minutes any more, so on a cold day we take chairs, and if that looks wrong to anybody it can look wrong.

If you served and you are able to stand and hold a rifle, we will teach you the rest of it in two Saturday mornings.

blocks.text: The government marker, and the paperwork

blocks.body:
[b]A grave marker for a veteran is free from the government.[/b] What costs money is setting it, and that is a stone mason's bill and not a marker bill. If somebody has quoted you one price for the whole thing, ask which part of it is the marker.

A burial in the village cemetery needs a permit from the village clerk, who is in the office at 22 Front Street on Tuesdays from nine to eleven. There is a form and there is no fee. Two hours a week is what that office is, and every funeral home in three counties knows it.

Death certificates come from the county clerk, and [url=synth://verity.county.gov/s/records]the county's records page[/url] has what it costs and what to bring. The service officer will sit with you and do the VA burial allowance form on a Thursday morning, which takes about forty minutes and is free, and the outfits that telephone widows offering to do it for a percentage are not doing anything you cannot do at this table.

Gene Hoke's death notice on the Ledger's website in September gave his post as American Legion Post 219 and gave the date of death as 18 September, which is the day the funeral home filed it. He was a member here for 51 years and he died on the 16th.

The family asked for a correction. What came back was the same notice with the date changed and the post still wrong. It is still wrong. [url=synth://now.verityledger.com/corrections]Their corrections page[/url] does not carry it.

So: what is on this page is what this post has in its own book, and the book is on paper, and if you see something about one of ours somewhere else that does not match this page, this page is right.
[i]Last changed Tuesday 13 October 2026. -- N.P.[/i]

41 members. Meets the third Tuesday at 6:30 downstairs and is finished by half past seven, which the post has never once managed.

Eligibility is the same family relationship it has always been, and since 2015 it takes men, and we have four. Dues are $30. Bonnie Speck is president, Deb Osterhout is secretary, and Marlene Vore has been treasurer since 2011 and would like somebody to learn the book.

blocks.text: There are three auxiliaries in this village and they are not the same thing

blocks.body:
This gets mixed up constantly, including by people who have lived here their whole lives, so here it is written down.

[b]This one[/b] is the VFW Auxiliary to Post 6791. Poppies, the relief fund, the children's Christmas party, the dish room on a Friday.

[b]The Milbrook Fire Department Ladies Auxiliary[/b] does the roast beef dinner in October and the rescue tool fund. Doris Ballou ran it for years and Sheryl Ruhl has it now.

[b]The Milbrook Ladies Auxiliary[/b] is the one with the election day pie sale at the village hall, which has been going since 1974 and which started at the Methodist church.

We help each other with tables and urns and nobody keeps score. If you send a cheque to the wrong one, whoever gets it will walk it over.

Two Saturdays in May, outside the post office in the morning and outside the bank in the afternoon, and one more Saturday at the library book sale in November.

[b]$1,842 this year.[/b] That was $2,310 in 2019 and it is not because people got less generous, it is because there are fewer people going past and more of them have no cash on them. Four people in May handed over a card and we had to say we could not take it.

Every dollar of it goes in the relief fund. The poppies themselves are made by disabled veterans and are paid for out of the Auxiliary's own account, not out of what is collected.

blocks.text: What the relief fund actually paid for

blocks.body: Twelve months to 30 September 2026. No names, and Marlene writes them in the book by number.

items: A car battery and the labour, $186. He had the interview on the Tuesday.
A fuel oil delivery of 100 gallons in February, $340, for a widow who had been running the kerosene heater in one room.
Two prescriptions the insurance would not cover until the appeal came back, $214 the pair.
A furnace igniter and the service call, $265.
A month's lot rent, $310, once, for a family that is now current.
Four rides to the VA hospital at 62 cents a mile, $228 altogether, paid to the members who drove.
$400 to the Milbrook fire company's own fund after the Sixth Street fire in March, because they came for one of ours in 2024.
Groceries, $412 in fifteen separate goes, which is what the fund mostly is.

blocks.body:
$2,355 out. The fund had $3,104 in it on 30 September.

[b]How you ask.[/b] Telephone the hall, or tell any member, or tell Bonnie at the fish fry. There is no form, no proof of income, and no committee meeting about you. Two people decide and one of them is the treasurer, and it is done that day if it needs to be.

It is for veterans and their families first. Nobody has ever been sent away because they turned out not to be a veteran and we are not going to start.

Voice of Democracy is for high school and Patriot's Pen is for grades six through eight. Post prizes are $100 and $50, and the post winner goes to district.

We had 40 entries in 2011 and we had [b]9[/b] this year. That is not the children. The English teacher at Kerrin who ran it for twenty years retired in 2022 and nobody told the person who replaced her that it existed, and it took us three years to work out that this was what had happened. Deb walked into the school in September with the forms and a plate of cookies and we expect a better number this year.

Entries are due to the hall by 31 October. Any student in the district, whether or not anybody in the family served.

blocks.body:
If you are the spouse, parent, child, grandchild, sibling or grandparent of somebody eligible for the VFW, you are eligible for this. Bring the veteran's discharge paper or the number off it and Marlene will do the rest at the table.

We are 41 and we were 96 in 2004. The dish room needs two more people on a Friday and the poppy table needs somebody who can stand outside for two hours in May.
[i]Last changed Tuesday 13 October 2026, from what Marlene wrote out at the September meeting. -- N.P.[/i]

[b]This is not a newspaper and it is not trying to be one.[/b]

The [url=synth://milbrookgazette.com/]Milbrook Gazette[/url] printed every Thursday from April 1908 to [b]Thursday 27 October 2016[/b]. The note in the last edition said the break would be short. Dean Rask meant it when he wrote it.

This page began in 2017 as three lines about hall dates. People started telephoning the hall with things that had nowhere else to go, so it is what it is now. There is no charge, there never has been, and there is not going to be.

[b]To put something on it:[/b] tell Wanda on a Tuesday or Thursday morning, telephone 782-6612 and leave it on the machine, or write it on the pad by the canteen door. Say it the way you want it printed. We will not print anything about a person that the person did not ask us to print, we will not print politics beyond the time and place of a meeting, and we will not print anything for sale over $200 because that is what [url=synth://classifieds.verity.net/]the classifieds[/url] are for.

[b]40 copies of this page are printed every other Tuesday[/b] and left at the post office, the bank, the hardware store and the library, because about half of this village is not reading a website and that half is the half this page is for.

[b]Hydrant flushing, Tuesday 3 November to Thursday 5 November.[/b] The village will work Front and Second on the Tuesday, Oak and Dunmore on the Wednesday, and Bethel Road and the outside lines on the Thursday. Your water may run rusty for an hour or two after the crew has been past. Run the cold tap until it clears before you put a wash in, because it will stain and the village will not pay for it. There is no advisory and nothing is wrong with the water.

[b]Leaf pickup.[/b] Mondays, 19 October through 23 November. To the curb, not in the street, not in bags. The village will not take brush with the leaves and has not since 2019, and the brush day is the first Monday in April.

[b]Blood drive in this hall, Thursday 8 October, 1:00 to 6:00.[/b] Walk in or book. They wanted 37 units and got 41 and the woman running it says the north end is the best draw in the county per head, and has said so for four years.

They are back Thursday 4 February.

[b]There is no flu clinic in Milbrook this autumn.[/b] The nearest is the Coyne Flats Grange hall, 7 Grange Road, Thursday 5 November, 10:00 a.m. to 1:00 p.m. Flu shot is $25 and free if you are 65 or over or on public assistance. Bring your card if you have it.

The Health Department's page says the Milbrook clinic "was not scheduled because the room is not available and no alternative was offered." We offered this hall in writing on Friday 14 August, for nothing, with the kitchen and the parking, and what came back was an automatic acknowledgement with a reference number on it. We telephoned on 2 September and pressed option 3 and it rang out, which we have since learned is a known fault with their telephone menu. We will offer again in the spring and we will telephone a person next time.

Coyne Flats is 23 miles from here and [url=synth://verity-transit.gov/s/dial-a-ride]Dial-A-Ride[/url] will take you and will wait, but you have to be registered and you have to book by the day before. If you are not registered and need to be, come to the hall on a Thursday morning and the service officer will do the form with you over the telephone.

[b]Milbrook Free Library book sale, Saturday 7 November, nine to two, in the basement.[/b] Paperbacks a quarter, hardcovers a dollar. The box of National Geographics is free and has been free and will be there again next year.

They want help carrying tables up on the Friday evening at six. Four people did it last year and two of them are over eighty.

[b]Kerrin Consolidated school board[/b] meets Tuesday 20 October at 7:00 in the high school library. On the agenda is the bus contract and the Tessler run. It is open and anybody may speak for three minutes at the start, and you do not have to sign up beforehand whatever the sheet on the door says.

[b]Gene Hoke died on Wednesday 16 September at home on Oak Street.[/b] He was 88 and a member of this post for 51 years. The service was at Zion Lutheran on the Saturday and the family has asked us to thank everybody who brought food to the house, which they say was more food than the house has seen since the funeral before this one.

His notice on the Ledger's website has the wrong date and the wrong post and the family has given up on it. What is right is on [url=/taps]the Post Everlasting page[/url].

[b]Found[/b] in the hall lot after the rental on Saturday 26 September: a set of car keys on a brass fob with a letter R on it. They are in the office. Telephone 782-6612 or ask at the canteen.

[b]Wanted.[/b] Somebody with a pickup to take the old ice machine away. It is 300 pounds, it is on a pallet by the back door, and it is free to whoever loads it. We listed it in [url=synth://classifieds.verity.net/]the classifieds[/url] in July and got two replies and neither of them came.

[b]The food pantry van from St Mark's in Marchfield comes to Milbrook on the fourth Thursday of the month[/b] and it will bring a box to your door. Telephone their office by the Tuesday before. Milbrook has had no pantry of its own since 2019. The fire company keeps a box at the station and somebody is usually there on a Monday evening, and there is a shelf in the canteen here with the plain things on it that anybody may take, no questions, whether or not you are a member.

[url=synth://stmarks-verity.org/pantry]Their page[/url] has the hours, what they are short of, and the delivery route.

[b]Three members have had the veterans benefit letter this month.[/b] It is a letter, or sometimes a telephone call, saying that surviving family members in Verity County may be entitled to unclaimed memorial benefits and that the filing window is closing. It points at [url=synth://veterans-memorial-claim.win/]veterans-memorial-claim[/url] and it wants a social security number and a card.

There is no such window and there are no such benefits. The real VA burial allowance is a form, it is free, and the service officer at this hall will do it with you on a Thursday morning. The sheriff's office keeps a running list of what is going around at [url=synth://veritysheriff.gov/s/scams]their scams page[/url] and this one is on it.

If you already gave them something, telephone the bank first and the sheriff's office second, and do not be embarrassed about it, because one of the three who got it this month is a retired bank teller.

[b]The clock on the front of the bank has now said 4:20 for ten years.[/b] Bernice Kolb wrote it up in the Gazette in October 2016 and was told at the counter that it was a regional matter. It is still a regional matter. The branch is open Tuesday and Thursday, ten to three.

We are not campaigning about a clock. We are noting it, because that is what this page is for and because somebody asked us to.

[b]Where these notices end up.[/b] What went on this page on 30 September as a line about hydrant flushing came back three days later on one of the county news sites as "Milbrook Water Main Break Prompts Advisory." There is no break and there is no advisory. The piece named no one, quoted no one, and had a byline on it that is not a person.

Ruth Cannady at [url=synth://thequarry.news/]The Quarry[/url] telephoned the village clerk about it and printed one sentence saying it was routine flushing, which is one more sentence of checking than the site that ran it did. [url=synth://brenners-notebook.email/]Hal Brenner[/url] mentioned it too.

We are leaving our notices up anyway. The answer to a machine copying you badly is not to stop writing things down.

[i]Notices are cleared off this page after about eight weeks. Karen Fennimore at [url=synth://marchfieldlibrary.blog/]the Marchfield library[/url] asked in March whether anybody was keeping them, and now Wanda puts the printed sheet in a binder and it goes to the library once a year, which took about four minutes to arrange and which nobody had thought of in nine years.[/i]
[i]Last changed Friday 9 October 2026. -- N.P.[/i]

blocks.text: The post, the building, and who does what

blocks.caption: The charter in the entry, 28 August 1946, 61 names. The frame is the original and the glass is not.

blocks.body: The books are audited every May by three members who hold no office. The audit is one page and it is read out at the June meeting whether anybody wants it read out or not. Roger has signed the cheques since 2009 and asks every year for somebody to learn it, and this year Mark said he would, which is the first time anybody has.

head: Members
rows: The most there has ever been.
Average age 74. Eleven are life members who no longer come.

blocks.body:
Dues are $45 a year, payable by 31 December. Life membership is on the age-scaled table and runs from $400 down, and Roger has that on a sheet.

[b]Eligibility, plainly.[/b] You have to have served in a foreign war, campaign or expedition and have the campaign medal, the expeditionary medal, or hostile fire or imminent danger pay to show it. That is the whole of it and that is what makes this different from the Legion.

If you are not sure, bring your DD-214 to the hall on a Tuesday morning and Dennis will tell you in five minutes. If it turns out you are not eligible here you are very likely eligible at [b]Legion Post 219[/b], which is four streets away on Oak, and one of us will walk over with you and introduce you, because a veteran standing in a parking lot with his discharge paper in his hand is a failure whichever building it happens outside of.

Alan Sluyter is here Thursday mornings, 9:00 to 11:30, and he is not a lawyer and he does not charge anything.

What he does is sit with you and fill in the form. Disability claims, the burial allowance, Aid and Attendance, the appeal when the first answer is no, ordering a replacement discharge paper, and finding the medal somebody's father threw in a drawer in 1954. [b]31 claims this year[/b], of which nine are still open, and he has a folder for each one because the Regional Office loses things.

You do not have to be a member of anything. Two of the people he is working with now are not veterans at all, they are widows.

[b]Nobody should ever pay a percentage of backpay to have a claim filed.[/b] There are outfits advertising to do exactly that and one of them is buying advertising against this county's name. The accredited service officer route costs nothing, and if Alan cannot do it he will send you to the county veterans service agency in Gridfall, which also costs nothing.

Block, 1962, put up over fourteen Saturdays by the membership on a lot the village sold to the post for a dollar. The men who poured the floor are on a list in the safe and there are two of them still living.

The panelling went up in 1978. There has been a vote about painting it twice, in 2019 it lost 31 to 24, and in 2024 it lost 28 to 19. The trend is clear and the panelling will outlast several of us.

The roof was done in 2011, membrane over the flat part, and it has three or four years left in it. Nobody has priced it since 2024 and the number then was $28,000. The boiler is 1984 and is serviced in September by Bortner Propane, who say the same thing about it every year.

The ramp and the wide door went in in 2009, paid for out of a memorial. The stage still has three steps and no way up for a chair, which is the single worst thing about this building.

The honor roll board in the entry is the 1946 one, 214 names, with a second panel added in 1968. Gold stars are hand painted and the last one added was in 1970. Karen Fennimore at the Marchfield library found the Ledger's notice of our charter on the microfilm in February and photocopied it for us and would not take anything for it, and it is in the case under the board.

blocks.body:
These are round numbers off the quartermaster's report and the exact ones are in the book, which any member may read at any meeting and which four members did last year.

The short version is that this post runs on the hall and the fryer. Dues cover the insurance and about six weeks of heat.

Put up in 2009 by Roger's grandson, who was in eleventh grade and who is now in Michigan with two children and answers within a day when I email him, which is more than I deserve.

It cost $0 to build and it costs $96 a year to keep. It moved hosts in 2021 when the first one stopped answering the telephone, and the only thing lost in the move was a photograph gallery from the 2012 parade that was in some format nothing opens now.

I change the words. I do not change anything else, because in 2018 I changed something else and the left side of every page went away for two days. There are six pages of instructions in a folder in the office, written in 2009, and four of them are still correct.

Anything on this site that is wrong is mine. Telephone the hall on a Tuesday morning and tell me and I will fix it that week. -- Neil Prosser, adjutant.

The last two of those have not gone anywhere in years. The Business Association wound up in 2014 when there were four businesses left to be in it. I have left both buttons where they are because taking them off does not bring anything back.
The form was turned off in June 2019 after it filled up twice in one night. The entries that are left are left because the only way I can find to remove them is to remove the whole box.
